title: Fallback Context Matrix Brainbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick, messy working notes for a lightweight client-side + runtime fallback matrix that can express cost/latency/quality tradeoffs per call. Intended as a minimal API shape + config the client SDK can ship with (v0) and a runtime routing policy that uses it.

Goals (non-exhaustive):
- Let calling app express SLO profile (latency budget, quality floor, cost cap) per request
- Prefer cached/prefix/KV responses when available, then quantized fast variants, then full model->region fallback
- Keep client API tiny (3 fields) so product teams can adopt without deep infra changes
- Enable telemetry tagging so we can measure fallthrough rates and quality regressions

Quick sketch: API shape (request-level metadata)
{
  "slo_profile": "laggard|balanced|interactive",    // semantic presets for defaults
  "latency_ms": 400,                              // soft SLO in ms (optional)
  "cost_limit_micro": 200000,                      // micro-units per request (optional)
  "quality_floor": "p95_similarity>0.8"           // simple expression language for quality guard (optional)
}

Fallback matrix (runtime interpretable):
- Stage A: Client local cache / prefix cache lookup (ttl, shard-key)
  - If hit and similarity >= quality_floor -> return with tag "cache-hit"
- Stage B: In-region fast quantized variant (q8) -> tag "fast-quant"; target p50 latency <= latency_ms * 0.5
- Stage C: Dedicated pool (higher cost) -> tag "dedicated"; fallback to burst-capacity when autoscale not ready
- Stage D: Cross-region fallback (if latency budget allows) -> tag "cross-region"
- Stage E: Degraded streaming-mode response (truncate long generations) -> tag "truncated"
- Stage F: Graceful error with best-effort summary of last good output -> tag "degraded-error"

Policy semantics:
- Each stage has selectors: {compat_models, estimated_ms, estimated_cost_micro, success_rate_est}
- Router computes cheapest compatible stage where estimated_ms <= latency_ms AND estimated_cost_micro <= cost_limit_micro. If none meet all constraints, pick stage that maximizes (quality_est * weight_quality + inverse_cost * weight_cost) where weights derive from slo_profile preset.

Config example (YAML-ish) for a tenant policy (v1):
fallback_policies:
  default:
    slo_presets:
      interactive: {weight_quality: 0.6, weight_cost: 0.2, weight_latency: 0.2}
      balanced:    {weight_quality: 0.5, weight_cost: 0.3, weight_latency: 0.2}
      laggard:     {weight_quality: 0.3, weight_cost: 0.5, weight_latency: 0.2}
    stages:
      - name: local-cache
        type: cache
        max_age_s: 86400
      - name: fast-quant
        model_tags: [gptx-lite-q8, small-synth]
        est_ms: 60
        est_cost_micro: 5000
      - name: dedicated
        model_tags: [gptx-8b, gptx-13b-rt]
        est_ms: 120
        est_cost_micro: 25000
      - name: cross-region
        region_fallback_order: [eu-west1, us-central1]
        cost_multiplier: 1.15

Telemetry fields to emit per request:
- chosen_stage, chosen_model, estimated_ms, actual_ms, estimate_error_pct, cost_micro_charged, quality_metric_value, fallback_chain (list of attempted stages)

ASCII routing diagram (very rough):
Client -> local-cache? --hit--> Client (cache-hit)
                 
                 --miss--> Ingress router -> fast-quant pool -> if fail/slow -> dedicated pool -> if saturated -> cross-region -> final degrade

Open questions / TODOs:
- Quality_floor expression: design DSL vs simple named metrics (similarity, BLEU, safety-score). Start with named metrics to avoid slow parsing.
- Client SDK: should we expose slo_profile only, or full latency_ms/cost_limit? Start with profile + optional latency_ms.
- How to bootstrap est_cost_micro/est_ms? Use historical rolling windows per model+region; default fallbacks if no data. Need cold-start plan.
- RBAC/tenancy: allow tenant overrides but global guardrails from infra-team. Need enforcement surface.
- Compatibility matrix: need a small catalog mapping model variants -> compatible payloads (tool-calls, streaming, long-context)
- Metrics: baseline fallthrough rate per route and quality degradation delta; ship an alert when stage E/F > 3% for a route over 1h.

Notes to self: keep v0 minimal so SDK can ship quickly. Prototype with two presets (interactive, balanced) + optional latency_ms field. Implement telemetry first.

Meeting followups: loop in observability (Luis) to define metric names, and product (Samira) for UX presets; ask infra for cold-start defaults and a simple admin UI for stage ordering edits.

Rough estimate: prototyping (4 wks) + deploy canary to 2 routes (6 wks) -> measure fallback rates + iterate.

End of brainbook.
